slides.title: Navigating the User Interface
slides.text:
SEARCH BAR

This tool helps GEE users quickly access datasets and zoom to locations

slides.title: Navigating the User Interface
slides.text:
LEFT PANEL

- SCRIPT: In this tab, any script you save will be listed under “Owner”.
- DOCS: In this tab, you will see a categorical listing of available functions to use as you write your script.
- ASSETS: Any files that you have uploaded to or exported to GEE will be listed in this tab.

slides.title: Navigating the User Interface
slides.text:
CODE EDITOR

All GEE scripts are written in javascript and can be activated by clicking the “Run” button or pressing ctrl-enter (cmd-enter on Mac). A word of caution:  it is not automatically save!

  - code editor

slides.title: Navigating the User Interface
slides.text:
RIGHT PANEL

- INSPECTOR: The mouse cursor changes to a crosshairs and             clicking on the map allows us to sample our data from a particular latitude and longitude.
- CONSOLE: This is the default tab when GEE loads and contains helpful information related to data being accessed in the script             editor as well as statistical printouts and error messages.
- TASKS: In this tab, we can track the progress of any data that are in the queue for export/download.

slides.title: Navigating the User Interface
slides.text:
MAP VIEWER

- GEOMETRY TOOL: (upper left corner of the map) The hand icon is the cursor for panning around the map. Users can then import geometries to your script by drawing them on the screen. You can draw geometries for:
- points
- lines
- polygons
- rectangles
- LAYER PANEL: (upper right corner of the map) This drop down is used to adjust the display of layers you added to the map.

  - Map viewer

slides.title: Intro to JavaScript in GEE
slides.text:
COMMENT

- DOUBLE SLASH (//): for indicating a line of code is a comment, to explain the code or leave a note for yourself.
- The Code Editor also provides a shortcut— Ctrl + / on Windows, Cmd + / on Mac —to comment or uncomment multiple lines at a time.
- // This is comment!

slides.title: Intro to JavaScript in GEE
slides.text:
PRINT FUNCTION

- Print is a function to print text or further information, where the output will be displayed on the upper right-hand panel under the Console after clicking the Run button
- print(‘Hello World’)

If you want to filter a specific area, you need to check the attribute you want to filter by

Let’s go to: https://code.earthengine.google.com/ Let’s try to display the words “Hello World”

slides.title: Intro to JavaScript in GEE
slides.text:
VARIABLE (var)

LISTS

- A variable is a storage location in programming that holds data that can be changed or manipulated.
- var city = ‘Johor’
- NOTE: The code below assigns the text “Manila” to the variable named city. Single quotes (‘) or Double quotes (“) on either side of the text can be used to create a text string in the code.

- JavaScript provides a data structure called a list that can hold multiple values. We can create a new list using the square brackets [  ] and adding multiple values separated by a comma (,). This example is a list of strings of city names assigned to the variable cities.
- var cities = [‘Johor', ‘Kedah', ‘Kelantan', ‘Melaka'];print(cities);

Let’s go to: https://code.earthengine.google.com/ Let’s try to display “var” and list “[ ]”

- WORKING WITH IMAGES
- Images are composed of one or more bands and each band has its own name, data type, scale, mask and projection

slides.title: Asset Types
slides.text:
- RASTER
- Image
  - A single raster image
  - May have multiple bands, properties*
- ImageCollection
  - Indexed during creation
  - Supports filtering and aggregation of many images by time, area, etc.

- TABLE
- FeatureCollection
  - Geometry column inferred
    - Empty MultiPoint if missing
  - Other columns → Feature properties
  - Property/column keys:table.getInfo().columns

* All collections & elements can have key→value properties
